title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using a static IP address to access APIs.
summary: When third-party systems require a static IP address for API calls to Business Central, a common solution uses an Azure Function with a virtual network NAT gateway to route traffic through a fixed outbound IP. This approach bypasses the limitation that SaaS environments have dynamic IP addresses.
key_points: SaaS Business Central uses dynamic IP addresses, which conflicts with third-party systems requiring static IPs for firewall allowlisting
Azure Service Tags are the recommended solution, but not all third-party systems support them
An Azure Function in Premium or Flex Plan acts as a middleware to route requests and can be assigned a static IP via a NAT gateway
Configure virtual network integration in the Function app and set WEBSITE_VNET_ROUTE_ALL environment variable to 1 to route all outbound traffic through the VNET
A NAT gateway with a public IP address ensures all API responses to third-party systems originate from a single static IP

quotes.text: this scenario is not possible on a SaaS environment because the IP addresses of a Dynamics 365 Business Central tenant are not fixed
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core problem that triggers the need for this solution

quotes.text: A possible solution is to use an Azure Function as a middle layer between the third-party system and Dynamics 365 Business Central.
quotes.why_it_matters: Introduces the recommended workaround for the static IP requirement

quotes.text: The Azure Function must be deployed in the Premium Plan or in the new Flex plan to be able to support this scenario.
quotes.why_it_matters: Specifies the critical requirement for using NAT gateway with Azure Functions
